The norm comparison is sharp and fully proved: \(N(z)\le\|z\|_2\) follows termwise from Cauchy--Schwarz, while \(\|z\|_2\le\sqrt{4-2\sqrt2}\,N(z)\) follows from the eight explicit vertices of the unit ball. For \(x,y\in S_{X_8}\), the latter comparison and the Euclidean parallelogram identity give the global lower bound \((2+\sqrt2)/4\). The explicit unit pair \(x=(1,0)\), \(y=(2^{-1/2},2^{-1/2})\) attains that value. The checker independently confirms the exact algebraic equalities; no finite sampling is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: PASS. The regular octagon is a canonical symmetric absolute normalized norm between the square and Euclidean disk, while the lower Gao constant detects uniform non-squareness and is the central invariant of the motivating 2022 paper. The exact value is therefore a natural benchmark rather than an arbitrary slice. The result also shows that the published sufficient equality condition for the Euclidean-comparison lower bound is not necessary, because equality occurs here despite failure of that condition.
